data.title: PHP 8.5 adds pipe operator
data.author: lemper
data.article_summary: PHP 8.5将引入管道操作符（|>），这是一个期待已久的特性。管道操作符允许将左侧的值传递给右侧的函数，从而简化代码编写，尤其在链式操作中非常有用。例如，它可以将嵌套函数调用或使用临时变量的多步骤操作简化为流畅的管道形式，类似于Unix/Linux命令行中的管道。该特性灵感来源于函数式编程语言如F#和OCaml，最初由Facebook的HHVM/Hack引入PHP社区。经过多次提案和修订，最终在2025年由Larry Garfield等人成功实现并加入PHP 8.5。管道操作符虽然看似简单，但极大提升了代码的可读性和表达能力。

不同观点：
• rogue7：赞赏PHP的管道操作符，但提到Koka语言的点选择语法更简洁。他认为大多数语言无法实现这种语法，因为点符号已有其他用途。
• zelphirkalt：对PHP引入现代特性表示惊讶，认为这次改进不错，避免了引入新表达式类型可能带来的问题。

• bapak：提到JavaScript社区对管道操作符的期待，但该提案仍处于早期阶段。
• abrookewood：赞赏管道操作符，认为它使得代码更易读，相比传统的嵌套函数调用，管道操作符更直观。
• gbalduzzi：喜欢管道操作符，但不太喜欢...语法，特别是在与展开操作符混合使用时。
• sandreas：虽然欣赏管道操作符的尝试，但更偏好Kotlin的扩展函数或C#的迭代器方法，认为这些方法更简洁。

44794271.article_content:
banner text stub
PHP 8.5 Adds Pipe Operator: What it means
Published on
Jul 11, 2025
by
Larry Garfield
Stories
PHP 8.5, due out November of this year, will bring with it another long-sought-after feature: the
pipe operator
(
|>
).  It's a small feature with huge potential, yet it still took years to happen.
What is a pipe operator?
The pipe operator, spelled
|>
, is deceptively simple.  It takes the value on its left side and passes it as the single argument to a function (or in PHP's case,
callable
) on its right side:
$result = "Hello World" |> strlen(...)
// Is equivalent to
$result = strlen("Hello World");
On its own, that is not all that interesting.  Where it becomes interesting is when it is repeated, or chained, to form a "pipeline."  For example, here's real code from a real project I've worked on, recast to use pipes:
$arr = [
new Widget(tags: ['a', 'b', 'c']),
new Widget(tags: ['c', 'd', 'e']),
new Widget(tags: ['x', 'y', 'a']),
];
$result = $arr
|> fn($x) => array_column($x, 'tags') // Gets an array of arrays
|> fn($x) => array_merge(...$x)       // Flatten into one big array
|> array_unique(...)                  // Remove duplicates
|> array_values(...)                  // Reindex the array.
;
// $result is ['a', 'b', 'c', 'd', 'e', 'x', 'y']
The same code without pipes would require either this horribly ugly nest of evil:
array_values(array_unique(array_merge(...array_column($arr, 'tags'))));
Or manually creating a temporary variable for each step.  While temp variables are not the worst thing in the world, they are extra mental overhead, and mean that a chain like that cannot be used in a single-expression context, like a
match()
block.  A pipe chain can.
Anyone who has worked on the Unix/Linux command line will likely recognize the similarity to the shell pipe,
|
.  That's very deliberate, as it is effectively the same thing: Use the output from the left side as the input on the right side.
Where did it come from?
The
|>
operator appears in many languages, mostly in the functional world.  F# has essentially the exact same operator, as does OCaml.  Elixir has a slightly fancier version (which we considered but ultimately decided against for now).  Numerous PHP libraries exist in the wild that offer similar capability with many extra expensive steps, including my own
Crell/fp
.
The story for PHP pipes, though, begins with Hack/HHVM, Facebook's PHP fork née competitive implementation.  Hack included many features beyond what PHP 5 of the day offered; many of them eventually ended up in later PHP versions.  One of its features was a unique spin on a pipe operator.
In 2016, Sara Golemon, long-time PHP contributor and former Open Source lead on the HHVM project, proposed porting
Hack's pipes
to PHP directly.  In that RFC, the right side of a pipe wasn't a
callable
but an expression, and used a magic
$$
token (lovingly called
T_BLING
, at least according to yours truly) to inject the left-side result into it.  In that case, the example above would look like this:
$result = $arr
|> array_column($$, 'tags')
|> array_merge(...$$)
|> array_unique($$)
|> array_values($$)
;
While powerful, it was also somewhat limiting.  It was very non-standard, unlike any other language.  It also meant a weird, one-off syntax for partially-calling functions that worked only when paired with pipes.
That RFC didn't go as far as a vote.  Nothing much happened for several years, until 2020/2021.  That's when I, fresh off of writing a book on functional programming in PHP that talked about function composition, decided to take a swing at it.  In particular, I partnered with a team to work on
Partial Function Application
(PFA) as a separate RFC from a more
traditional pipe
.  The idea was that turning a multi-parameter function (like
array_column()
above) into the single-parameter function that
|>
needed was a useful feature on its own, and should be usable elsewhere.  The syntax was a bit different than the Hack version, in order to make it more flexible:
some_function(?, 5, ?, 3, ...)
, which would take a 5-or-more parameter function and turn it into a 3 parameter function.
Sadly, PFA didn't pass due to some engine complexity issues, and that largely undermined the v2 Pipe RFC, too.  However, we did get a consolation prize out of it:
First Class Callables
(the
array_values(...)
syntax), courtesy Nikita Popov, were by design a "junior", degenerate version of partial function application.
Fast-forward to 2025, and I was sufficiently bored to take another swing at pipes.  This time with a better implementation with lots of hand-holding from Ilija Tovilo and Arnaud Le Blanc, both part of the PHP Foundation dev team, I was able to get it through.
Third time's the charm.
More than the sum of its parts
Above, we described pipes as "deceptively simple."  The implementation itself is almost trivial; it's just syntax sugar for the temp variable version, effectively.  However, the best features are the ones that can combine with othe

data.article_summary: 德克萨斯农工大学开发的CLARKE系统利用无人机影像和人工智能，在几分钟内快速评估飓风和洪水后的损害情况。该系统由计算机科学与工程博士生Tom Manzini和救援机器人专家Robin Murphy博士领导开发，可以在短短七分钟内评估2000户住宅的损毁情况，帮助应急响应人员迅速制定救援计划。CLARKE使用先进的计算机视觉和机器学习算法，生成详细的损害报告和绕行路线，特别适用于农村或难以到达的地区。该系统已经过超过21,000栋房屋的训练，并在2024年飓风季成功部署于佛罗里达和宾夕法尼亚。其快速评估能力显著加速了救灾响应，被视为改变游戏规则的工具。

44762035.article_content:
Science & Tech
AI Turns Drone Footage Into Disaster Response Maps In Minutes
A system developed at Texas A&M uses drone imagery and artificial intelligence to rapidly assess damage after hurricanes and floods, offering life-saving insights in minutes.
Jul 28, 2025
By
Lesley Henton
,
Texas A&M University Division of Marketing and Communications
4 min. read
CLARKE was trained on drone images from over 21,000 houses across 10 major disasters.
Credit: Texas A&M University College of Engineering
A tool developed at Texas A&M University is set to transform how emergency responders assess damage after disasters. The technology, known as CLARKE (Computer vision and Learning for Analysis of Roads and Key Edifices) uses artificial intelligence and drone imagery to evaluate damage to buildings, roads and other infrastructure in a matter of minutes.
CLARKE was created by a team of researchers led by Tom Manzini, a Ph.D. candidate in computer science and engineering, and
Dr. Robin Murphy
, a pioneer in the field of rescue robotics.
“This is the first AI system that can classify building and road damage from drone imagery at this scale and speed,” Murphy said. “We’re talking about assessing a neighborhood of 2,000 homes in just seven minutes. That kind of speed can save lives and resources.”
The system has already proven its value during the 2024 hurricane season, when it was deployed in Florida and Pennsylvania following Hurricanes Debby and Helene.
The Magic Of Machine Learning
The name CLARKE is a nod to science fiction writer Arthur C. Clarke’s quote: “Any sufficiently advanced technology is indistinguishable from magic.” According to Murphy, the name was inspired by drone pilots working with the system who began calling its machine-learning capabilities “magic.”
But there’s nothing mystical about the science behind it. CLARKE uses cutting-edge computer vision and machine-learning algorithms to analyze drone footage, overlay damage assessments on maps, and generate spreadsheets listing each structure’s address and damage level. For roadways, it even includes a Google Maps-style route planner that helps responders avoid impassable roads.
CLARKE doesn’t just tell you what’s damaged, it tells you how to get around that damage. That’s critical when every second counts.
Dr. Robin Murphy
Senior Professor of Computer Science and Engineering
Texas A&M University College of Engineering
In rural or hard-to-reach areas, traditional damage assessments can take days, delaying aid and complicating logistics. With CLARKE, officials could launch drones and receive a comprehensive damage report within minutes, dramatically accelerating response times.
“Rural counties often have lost wireless connectivity so they can’t send imagery to state and federal agencies for manual inspection,” Murphy said. “CLARKE empowers them to take immediate action.”
The system was trained on drone images from over 21,000 houses across 10 major disasters, including Hurricanes Harvey and Ian. This extensive dataset allows CLARKE to recognize a wide range of damage patterns, making it adaptable to different types of disasters, including hurricanes, floods and wildfires.
Training The Front Lines
While the technology itself is groundbreaking, its success depends on the people using it. Last month, more than 60 emergency responders from 38 agencies and eight private companies gathered in Tallahassee, Florida, for a two-hour awareness training session on CLARKE. JAPAN
Kyoto University team develops pain reliever comparable to morphine
The newly developed drug, Adriana, is a groundbreaking painkiller, which works on a completely different mechanism to morphine and other existing synthetic opioids.

Aug 5, 2025
A Kyoto University research team has developed a pain-reliever that is comparable to morphine but does not have serious side effects.
Morphine, often administered to cancer patients, has serious adverse effects such as breathing issues and addiction.
According to the team, the newly developed drug, Adriana, is a groundbreaking painkiller, which works on a completely different mechanism to morphine and other existing synthetic opioids. The drug has the potential to revolutionize pain control in the medical field, the team said.
The team also expects that the drug will help resolve the so-called opioid epidemic, in which a large number of deaths occur mainly due to overdoses of opioids.
Its findings were published in the online edition of the U.S. journal Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences.
When a person encounters a life-threatening situation, norepinephrine, an organic chemical secreted from the brain, suppresses pain.
For its study, the team focused on the human body regulating oversecretion of norepinephrine. By introducing a new research technology, the team succeeded in developing a drug blocking such a control function for the first time in the world.
In a clinical trial conducted at the Kyoto University Hospital between January 2023 and December 2024, the team confirmed the new drug's efficiency to a certain extent for patients including 20 who underwent lung cancer surgery.
The team plans to conduct a clinical trial in the United States for 400 postsurgery patients in 2026, aiming to put Adriana into practical use in 2028.
"We hope that the new drug will help cancer patients who previously had no choice but to use opioids live their lives without pain as well as a need to worry about addiction or serious side effects," Masatoshi Hagiwara, a professor at the university, said.

data.title: Lamport's Byzantine Generals Algorithm in Python
data.author: Maro
data.article_summary:
本文讨论了拜占庭将军问题的经典解决方案，该问题涉及在一个分布式系统中，部分节点可能出现任意故障或恶意行为（如撒谎、伪造信息），如何达成一致。假设有一组将军（节点），其中一些可能是叛徒（故障节点），他们需要就共同行动（如进攻或撤退）达成一致。解决方案需确保即使存在叛徒，忠诚的将军们仍能达成共识。

文章介绍了Lamport等人提出的口头消息算法：在有$N$个将军和最多$M$个叛徒的情况下，若超过三分之二的将军是忠诚的，问题可解。忠诚的将军需就同一行动达成一致，以确保胜利。文章还讨论了在现代计算机系统中的应用及假设，包括消息验证、叛徒行为模式及处理方式。核心挑战在于设计一种消息交换算法，使非叛徒节点能达成一致，即便提议的国王（发起算法的节点）可能是叛徒。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Lamport算法及其贡献的评价

不同观点：

• [潜在的中立观点] 评论中未涉及对算法本身的批评或质疑，但强调的重点在于Lamport的整体贡献和获奖情况，可能暗示其算法的影响力更多体现在学术认可上，而非直接的实际应用。

补充讨论：
• 图灵奖的提及作为对Lamport贡献的重要认可，具有很高的学术声望，表明讨论者关注的是Lamport在计算机科学领域的长期影响。
• 未提及算法的具体技术细节或应用实例，显示讨论更偏向于对其学术地位和行业认可的评价，而非技术实现的具体讨论。

44767163.article_content:
Introduction
Imagine a group of generals of the Byzantine army camped with their troops around an enemy city. The generals must agree upon a common battle plan: either attack or retreat. However, some of them may be traitors! The non-traitor generals succeed only if all of them choose the same action â either everyone attacks or everyone retreats; if even one non-traitor general does something different, the battle is lost.
In their seminal paper
The Byzantine Generals Problem
Lamport, Shostak and Pease pose this problem with the analogue of the Byzantine generals, and give solutions using distributed algorithms. Their abstract reads:
Reliable computer systems must handle malfunctioning components that give conflicting information to different parts of the system. This situation can be expressed abstractly in terms of a group of generals of the Byzantine army camped with their troops around an enemy city. Communicating only by messenger, the generals must agree upon a common battle plan. However, one or more of them may be traitors who will try to confuse the others. The problem is to find an algorithm to ensure that the loyal generals will reach agreement. It is shown that, using only oral messages, this problem is solvable if and only if more than two-thirds of the generals are loyal; so a single traitor can confound two loyal generals. With unforgeable written messages, the problem is solvable for any number of generals and possible traitors. Applications of the solutions to reliable computer systems are then discussed.
The problem asks: how can distributed processes reach agreement when a subset of them  â up to $M$ in a total of $N$ nodes â might behave arbitrarily, lying, omitting, or forging messages? Failures of this kind are called
Byzantine
because, like traitorous generals, they do not merely crash; they actively try to mislead the rest of the system.
In this article, we will implement Lamport's classic solution for the Byzantine Generals problem, referred to as the
oral messages
version of the problem; this is the version we are considering in this article.
The code is on
Github: mtrencseni/dca/byzantine
Problem statement
The problem statement in plain English is the following: there are $N$ generals, $M$ of which is a traitor or faulty. They need to agree on a common order, which is commonly taken to be the two values
attack
and
retreat
. One of the generals is the king, who proposes the initial value (attack or retreat) and kicks off the algorithm. Note that the king may also be a traitor! Furthermore, if the king is not a traitor, we want all the other non-traitor generals to follow the king's orders.
Note: in Lamport's paper, the term
commander
is used instead of king; however, I find Lamport's terminology confusing, because the term commander is re-used in later stages of the algorithm for other nodes as well. So in this discussion, I avoid the term commander altogether.
The assumption is that if all non-traitors generals attack at the same time, they will be victorious, otherwise they get defeated. If they all agree to retreat, that is also an acceptable outcome. The act of attacking or retreating in the analogue story of Byzantine Generals is irrelevant, the point is that they all agree on a value. In this sense, attack and retreat are arbitrary, the value can be an arbitrary string âÂ the point is that all non-traitors should agree on the same value.
The challenge is to find an algorithm for exchanging messages between the generals that fulfills these requirements.
Note that if we can assume that the king is not a traitor, the solution is trivial: the king just sends his orders (value) to the other generals, and they do what the king told them to do. The problem is only interesting if the king
may
be one of the $M$ traitors.
Assumptions
Translating the problem to the language of modern computers, we make the following assumptions:
There are $N$ nodes which communicate with each other by sending messages.
Of the $N$ total nodes, $M$ are traitors (malicious, faulty, misbehaving, down).
The non-traitor nodes do not know who the traitors are. The traitors can know of each other and can collude.
One of the nodes (the king) initiates the distributed algorithm with an initial value.
For all messages received, nodes can identify the sender node â traitors cannot spoof messages.
Non-traitor nodes follow the distributed algorithm given.
Traitor nodes do not follow the distributed algorithm, they can:
not send some or all messages
send duplicate messages
send malformed messages
send well-formed messages that do not follow the distributed algorithm
send messages with a delay
send messages out-of-order
In terms of implementation, most of the traitor behaviour must be handled at the software engineering level. For example, how long should non-traitor nodes wait for messages from other nodes, before they stop waiting and assume a default value in order to advance the algorithm?

Raspberry Pi Expands Embedded Lineup with Low-Cost Radio and Camera Modules
Jul 20, 2025 — by Giorgio Mendoza
389 views
Twitter
Facebook
LinkedIn
Reddit
Pinterest
Email
This month, Raspberry Pi launched two new components for embedded designs. The $4 Radio Module 2 adds Wi-Fi and Bluetooth to RP2040 and RP2350 projects, while the Camera Module 3 Sensor Assemblies offer a compact way to integrate Raspberry Pi’s 12MP camera into custom hardware.
Raspberry Pi notes that the Radio Module 2 integrates the Infineon
CYW43439
chip, the same component found in the Pico W and Pico 2 W. It delivers 2.4GHz Wi-Fi 4 and Bluetooth 5.2 (Classic and BLE), and is intended for use with RP2040 and RP2350-based systems. With castellated edge pads, a built-in PCB antenna, and a compact 16.5mm × 14.5mm footprint, it offers a simple and cost-effective path to wireless connectivity.
— ADVERTISEMENT —
Raspberry Pi Radio Module 2
(click image to enlarge)
The announcement highlights that the module includes modular radio certification, allowing developers to skip costly RF compliance testing. This helps reduce both development time and expense. The module is compatible with the Raspberry Pi Pico SDK and MicroPython, supporting a smooth path from prototype to production.
Raspberry Pi Camera Module 3 Variants
(click image to enlarge)
Alongside the radio module, Raspberry Pi has introduced the Camera Module 3 Sensor Assemblies for developers who need imaging capabilities in a smaller format than the full-sized module.
Raspberry Pi Camera Module 3
(click image to enlarge)
The assemblies use the same Sony IMX708 11.9MP sensor with Phase Detection Autofocus and are available in both visible-light and NoIR variants. Raspberry Pi mentions that customers can choose between a standard 75-degree or a wide 120-degree field of view, and that full schematics and a bill of materials are provided to support hardware integration. A small rear connector allows direct integration with custom boards.
Further Information
The
Radio Module 2
is available for $4.40 from
PiShop.US
and $3.99 from
Pimoroni
. The
Camera Module 3 Sensor Assembly
is listed at $21.95 on
PiShop.US
or $15.00 from
Vilros
, depending on the variant. According to the product pages, the Radio Module 2 will remain in production until at least January 2036, while the Camera Module 3 Sensor Assembly is expected to be supported through January 2030.

data.title: Typed languages are better suited for vibecoding
data.author: hosolmaz
data.article_summary: 作者表示，自从Claude Code推出后，他超过10年的编程习惯发生了变化。他现在更倾向于使用TypeScript、Rust和Go等语言管理项目，即便这些语言他并不完全精通，但借助AI工具，他依然能高效完成工作。作者认为，具有类型和编译特性的语言在使用AI工具（如Claude Code）时更具优势，因为它们提供了更高的安全性保障。相比Python，这些语言能让作者更快、更安全地处理大规模项目，即使代码更低级。例如，在TypeScript项目中，Claude Code确保代码在每次任务后都能编译通过，这提高了稳定性。作者预测，由于AI工具的普及，Python在公司生产部署中的使用率可能会下降，尽管他个人非常喜欢Python。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：LLM（大型语言模型）在编程中的应用及其在不同编程语言中的表现

不同观点：
• [woodruffw] 认为即使在不熟悉的编程语言（如TypeScript、Rust和Go）中进行项目管理，LLM也能表现出色。但他指出，开发者可能因为不熟悉该语言而难以判断代码质量，且容易高估LLM的能力。
• [timuckun] 支持使用强意见框架（如Rails）进行"氛围编码"（vibe coding），因为这些框架有统一的规范和结构，即使类型系统较弱，LLM也能表现良好。相比之下，Go等语言尽管有更强的类型系统，LLM的表现却不尽如人意。
• [Reubend] 对LLM生成的大量代码（如3-5k行）表示担忧，认为这样不可能产生高质量的代码库。
• [lukev] 指出LLM在TypeScript中常遇到的"自旋"（spin out）问题，即模型陷入错误循环，难以有效解决问题，通常与类型相关。
• [linkage] 质疑LLM在不同语言中的表现，认为需要实际评估来验证，而不是仅凭推测。他建议通过类型注释和验证工具来增强动态类型语言的编码效果。
• [herrington_d] 认为LLM在动态类型语言中表现更好，因为无需解决类型错误，节省了上下文令牌。但在复杂类型错误时，LLM可能难以修复并选择绕过问题。
• [reflectiveattn] 提出使用较少标点符号的语言能更有效地避免幻觉问题，并提供更多的向量操作空间。
• [jjcm] 偏好使用Go进行氛围编码，因为Go的冗长特性使得代码易读且LLM能保持严格性。
• [solatic] 认为编码的质量取决于提供给LLM的反馈机制，如静态分析和自动化测试，而不仅是类型系统。
• [misja111] 对比Python和Scala，发现LLM在Python中表现更好，而在Scala中即使简单任务也常出错。
• [exclipy] 希望LLM能像人类使用IDE一样利用类型信息，并期待下一代LLM能生成语法和类型正确的代码。
• [MutedEstate45] 强调结构化的反馈对LLM迭代的重要性，如Rust的"cargo check"提供明确的错误信息，而Python的运行时错误往往缺乏上下文。
• [sshine] 个人经验表明Rust的氛围编码效果好，但Haskell的效果不佳，认为类型系统对LLM的指导作用显著。
• [dominicrose] 不喜欢Rust的结果，认为其代码冗长且符号多，更偏好Ruby等动态类型语言的简洁性。
• [stared] 支持使用强类型和强静态分析工具（如ESLint和Ruff）来引导LLM编写更可靠的代码，并分享了具体的编码指南。

补充讨论：
• LLM在不同编程语言中的表现引发了争议，特别是关于静态类型和动态类型的优劣。
• 反馈机制和类型系统的强弱对LLM的表现有显著影响。
• 实际评估（evals）被多次提及，强调需要通过实际数据来验证LLM的能力。
• 个人偏好和项目需求在选择编程语言和使用LLM时起到重要作用。

争议的焦点：
• LLM在不同语言中的实际表现及其对代码质量的影响。
• 静态类型和动态类型语言对LLM编码的支持程度。
• 如何有效地提供反馈和约束以引导LLM生成高质量代码。

44780878.article_content:
This post has made it to the Hacker News front page
, see the discussion there.
My >10 year old programming habits have changed since
Claude Code
launched. Python is less likely to be my go-to language for new projects anymore. I am managing projects in languages I am not fluent in—TypeScript, Rust and Go—and seem to be doing pretty well.
It seems that typed, compiled, etc. languages are better suited for vibecoding, because of the safety guarantees. This is unsurprising in hindsight, but it was counterintuitive because by default I “vibed” projects into existence in Python since forever.
Paradoxically, after a certain size of project, I can move faster and safer with e.g. Claude Code + Rust, compared to Claude Code + Python, despite the low-levelness of the code
1
. This is possible purely because of AI tools.
For example, I refactored large chunks of our TypeScript frontend code at TextCortex. Claude Code runs
tsc
after finishing each task and ensures that the code compiles before committing. This let me move much faster compared to how I would have done it in Python, which does not provide compile-time guarantees. I am amazed every time how my 3-5k line diffs created in a few hours don’t end up breaking anything, and instead even increase stability.
LLMs are
leaky abstractions
, sure. But they now work well enough so that they solve the problem Python solved for me (fast prototyping), without the disadvantages of Python (lower safety guarantees, slowness, ambiguity
2
).
Because of this, I predict a decrease in Python adoption in companies, specifically for production deployments, even though I like it so much.
Some will say that was the case even without AI tools, and to that my response is: it depends.
↩
Arguably.
↩

data.title: How to make almost anything (2019)
data.author: teleforce
data.article_summary: D. Sculley，谷歌剑桥机器学习研究团队的负责人，参与课程以探索机器学习在设计和制造领域的应用，包括生物学和化学领域。他对其他制造形式及其跨领域机会感兴趣，并计划每周参与课程项目，从计算机辅助设计（CAD）和草图设计到嵌入式编程和网络等多个主题，最终完成一个最终项目。Sculley拥有丰富的机器学习经验，自2003年开始从事该领域，此前曾从事教育工作并拥有艺术专业背景。他乐于分享机器学习知识，并预计在项目中会犯不少错误。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：关于各类制造课程的内容、价值及局限性的讨论

不同观点：
• [sgnelson] 认为FabAcademy课程（由Neil Gershenfeld主导）的学生项目文档比课程本身更有趣，并提供了学生项目和 highlights 的链接，强调学生作品的多样性和创意。
• [low_tech_punk] 指出该课程源于MIT的HTMAA课程，并提供了课程网站和相关播客链接，补充了有关课程背景的信息。
• [car] 提到了MIT另一门有关合成生物学的课程"How to Grow (Almost) Anything"，认为该课程需要较高的时间投入，但非常有价值。
• [dhosek] 表达了对大学时期未参加工具制作课程的遗憾，认为即使是非工程专业的学生也应有机会参与类似课程。
• [criddell] 认为当前是个人制造的黄金时代，引用Neil Gershenfeld的书《Fab》来支持观点，并表示高质量的个人制造技术已经实现。
• [zakqwy] 分享了自己在2019年参加该课程的经历，强调课程涵盖了数字制造和微控制器，是一次非常棒的学习体验。
• [Animats] 将课程与TechShop时代对比，认为课程像快速浏览多个技能，但要在某个技能上达到精通需要更多时间，而大学时间通常较紧。
• [moron4hire] 批评课程内容过于狭窄，缺乏基础技能如木工、金属加工、管道、混凝土等，并指出当前技术文化过度贬低年长者的技能和经验，提倡更广泛的技能学习。
• [mannykannot] 认为课程虽然涵盖了生物学和化学，但忽略了空间探索这一最终前沿。
• [LarsDu88] 分享了自己在PCB设计上的经验，提到从中国定制PCB的价格因关税上涨，认为这是美国创业公司的机会。
• [westurner] 指出"Week 8: Molding and Casting"链接404错误，强调生物塑料的重要性，并提出其他材料周的建议如可编程材料、纳米自组装、AI材料设计。
• [jeffreyw128] 简单表示该课程是其大学时期最喜欢的课程。
• [globalnode] 感谢HN的推荐，认为课程看起来很有趣。
• [probably_wrong] 认为不包括缝纫的"几乎任何东西"课程是不完整的，并批评课程缺乏木工和焊接，建议改名为"如何制造一些需要电脑的东西"。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点在于课程内容的广度和深度，尤其是[moron4hire]和[probably_wrong]对课程缺乏基础技能和多样性的批评与其他参与者对课程创意性和前沿性的赞赏形成对比。
• 课程的具体实施和时间投入也是讨论的重要方面，[Animats]和[car]提到在有限时间内掌握多个技能的难度，[dhosek]则表达了对未参与某些实践课程的遗憾。
• 技术文化对年长者技能的贬低也被提及，[moron4hire]强调了传统技能的持久价值和与现代技术的结合。

这些观点展示了不同背景的参与者对制造课程的多元看法，涵盖了课程内容、技能价值和现代技术教育的方向。

44775830.article_content:
My name is D. Sculley.  I lead several teams at Google in
Cambridge doing research in various aspects of machine learning.
I'm involved in this course because many of our current projects involve
the use of machine learning for design or fabrication problems of
one form or another, including in the biology space and the chemistry
space.  I'm interested in learning more about other forms of fabrication
and seeing if there are interesting cross-domain opportunities to
think about.
Here is my
Google Scholar page
, if you're interested in ML papers.
As background, I started working in ML in about 2003.  Before that,
I spent several years in education working as a teacher, and before that
I was a V.E.S. ("art") major in undergrad.
I'll be working on class projects each week, and am planning on making
plenty of mistakes. Always happy to talk about machine learning if that's of interest.

CAD and Sketching
Week 2:
Laser and Vinyl Cutting
Week 3:

3D Scanning and Printing

Output Devices

44775830.article_summary: D. Sculley，谷歌剑桥机器学习研究团队的负责人，参与课程以探索机器学习在设计和制造领域的应用，包括生物学和化学领域。他对其他制造形式及其跨领域机会感兴趣，并计划每周参与课程项目，从计算机辅助设计（CAD）和草图设计到嵌入式编程和网络等多个主题，最终完成一个最终项目。Sculley拥有丰富的机器学习经验，自2003年开始从事该领域，此前曾从事教育工作并拥有艺术专业背景。他乐于分享机器学习知识，并预计在项目中会犯不少错误。
44775830.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：关于各类制造课程的内容、价值及局限性的讨论

不同观点：
• [sgnelson] 认为FabAcademy课程（由Neil Gershenfeld主导）的学生项目文档比课程本身更有趣，并提供了学生项目和 highlights 的链接，强调学生作品的多样性和创意。
• [low_tech_punk] 指出该课程源于MIT的HTMAA课程，并提供了课程网站和相关播客链接，补充了有关课程背景的信息。
• [car] 提到了MIT另一门有关合成生物学的课程"How to Grow (Almost) Anything"，认为该课程需要较高的时间投入，但非常有价值。
• [dhosek] 表达了对大学时期未参加工具制作课程的遗憾，认为即使是非工程专业的学生也应有机会参与类似课程。
• [criddell] 认为当前是个人制造的黄金时代，引用Neil Gershenfeld的书《Fab》来支持观点，并表示高质量的个人制造技术已经实现。
• [zakqwy] 分享了自己在2019年参加该课程的经历，强调课程涵盖了数字制造和微控制器，是一次非常棒的学习体验。
• [Animats] 将课程与TechShop时代对比，认为课程像快速浏览多个技能，但要在某个技能上达到精通需要更多时间，而大学时间通常较紧。
• [moron4hire] 批评课程内容过于狭窄，缺乏基础技能如木工、金属加工、管道、混凝土等，并指出当前技术文化过度贬低年长者的技能和经验，提倡更广泛的技能学习。
• [mannykannot] 认为课程虽然涵盖了生物学和化学，但忽略了空间探索这一最终前沿。
• [LarsDu88] 分享了自己在PCB设计上的经验，提到从中国定制PCB的价格因关税上涨，认为这是美国创业公司的机会。
• [westurner] 指出"Week 8: Molding and Casting"链接404错误，强调生物塑料的重要性，并提出其他材料周的建议如可编程材料、纳米自组装、AI材料设计。
• [jeffreyw128] 简单表示该课程是其大学时期最喜欢的课程。
• [globalnode] 感谢HN的推荐，认为课程看起来很有趣。
• [probably_wrong] 认为不包括缝纫的"几乎任何东西"课程是不完整的，并批评课程缺乏木工和焊接，建议改名为"如何制造一些需要电脑的东西"。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点在于课程内容的广度和深度，尤其是[moron4hire]和[probably_wrong]对课程缺乏基础技能和多样性的批评与其他参与者对课程创意性和前沿性的赞赏形成对比。
• 课程的具体实施和时间投入也是讨论的重要方面，[Animats]和[car]提到在有限时间内掌握多个技能的难度，[dhosek]则表达了对未参与某些实践课程的遗憾。
• 技术文化对年长者技能的贬低也被提及，[moron4hire]强调了传统技能的持久价值和与现代技术的结合。

这些观点展示了不同背景的参与者对制造课程的多元看法，涵盖了课程内容、技能价值和现代技术教育的方向。

data.title: uBlock Origin Lite now available for Safari
data.author: Jiahang
data.article_summary: uBO Lite (uBOL) 是一个基于浏览器扩展接口（Manifest Version 3）开发的内容屏蔽工具。它使用与 uBlock Origin 类似的预设过滤规则列表，包括 EasyList、EasyPrivacy 和 Peter Lowe 的广告与跟踪服务器列表。uBOL 的过滤规则完全声明式，不需要持续运行的扩展进程，通过 CSS/JS 注入进行内容过滤，由浏览器进行调度，更加可靠。仅在打开弹出面板或设置页面时才会生成扩展进程。开发者 Raymond Hill 声明该应用不会收集任何数据，且隐私处理可能根据功能使用情况有所不同。该应用适用于 iOS 18.0 或更高版本的 iPhone、iPadOS 18.0 或更高版本的 iPad、macOS 15.0 或更高版本的 Mac，以及 visionOS 2.0 或更高版本的 Apple Vision 设备。应用免费且支持隐私政策。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：uBlock Origin Lite在iOS平台上的可用性、功能表现及与其他广告拦截器的比较

不同观点：
• **关于应用的可用性**：
  - jwr和JoeriBe指出该应用在他们的地区不可用，显示“This app is currently not available in your country or region”。
  - uallo提供了非中国地区的下载链接，帮助其他用户解决地域限制问题。

• **关于应用的功能和兼容性**：
  - MortyWaves尝试安装和使用uBlock Origin Lite，但在启用扩展时遇到问题，无法在Safari设置中启用，质疑其在iOS上的兼容性。
  - freehorse提到原始版本的uBlock Origin在Orion浏览器上运行良好，并认为Safari作为默认浏览器的平台上拥有uBlock Origin Lite是有益的。
  - tux指出该应用需要iOS 18.0+，不支持旧版iOS，令人遗憾。

• **关于广告拦截器的比较**：
  - AnonHP提到Magic Lasso，并与其他广告拦截器（如AdGuard、NextDNS、Firefox Focus）进行比较，关注订阅费用和功能差异。
  - forgotoldacc推荐Adguard，并表示其使用效果良好，广告拦截效果显著。
  - operator-name通过测试比较uBlock Origin Lite和Adguard，发现uBlock Origin Lite在广告拦截测试中的得分更高。
  - vouaobrasil认为iOS上的内容拦截器普遍表现不佳，而uBlock Origin Lite是最好的选择。

• **关于用户体验和期望**：
  - Trattue希望能在其地区使用该应用，并希望iOS Firefox能支持扩展或至少能同步书签。
  - TheSilva分享了使用Testflight版本的体验，认为uBlock Origin Lite与其之前的设置（Firefox Focus配置为Safari的广告拦截提供者）相比没有太大区别，但对其未来发展充满期待。
  - sometimes_all对uBlock Origin Lite的实际使用效果表示满意，特别是其自定义过滤工具，能够解决其他拦截器无法处理的问题。

补充讨论：
- 用户对iOS平台上广告拦截器的需求和期望较高，尤其是对扩展功能和跨平台同步的支持。
- 不同用户对广告拦截器的功能、性能和费用有不同的关注点，反映出用户在选择广告拦截器时的多样化需求。
- 地域限制和版本兼容性是影响用户体验的重要因素，部分用户因地域问题无法直接下载和使用uBlock Origin Lite。

data.title: Where to find ideas
data.author: kiyanwang
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：如何发现和验证创业想法

不同观点：
• TrackerFF：认为通过在不同行业工作，可以接触到需要解决的问题，尤其是传统行业中未解决的问题。他不认为必须在FAANG或麦肯锡这样的公司工作才能发现这些机会。
• Lyngbakr：强调创始人需要深入体验潜在客户的需求，成为他们的一部分，而不仅仅是空想或理论化。他支持“解决自己痛点”的建议。
• wavemode：建议与潜在客户交谈，录下对话以供回顾，并强调通过原型测试来验证产品想法，因为人们通常不知道自己想要什么。
• z0r：通过分享一个视频链接，暗示可以通过外部资源获取创业想法。
• lelanthran：简洁指出通过实际行动发现想法。
• cjs_ac：认为软件工程的核心在于如何表示问题和解决方案的细节，而不仅仅是编码。他强调深入领域知识的重要性，并建议离开大公司去小公司寻找未被发现的问题。
• andrewstuart：指出新的创业机会存在于社会、商业或技术变革中，并建议复制或竞争于Hacker News上看到的最佳创意。
• secretsatan：讽刺地建议从下属那里窃取想法。
• antonkar：提到一个声称通过三年模型预测未来并分享创业想法的资源。
• boredemployee：认为大多数人已经在解决某些问题，但成功往往依赖于运气、影响力、网络和时机等因素，且提到现实中存在诸如游说和继承财富等影响。
• begueradj：指出一些工作场所要求在特定会议上提出新想法，但认为想法如果不实施就毫无价值。
• noelwelsh：批评使用人身攻击来贬低他人方法的做法，并为诸如“市场需求”和“未被满足的利基”等概念辩护。

补充讨论：
• 争议的焦点之一是如何有效地发现和验证创业想法，一些人强调实际体验和客户反馈，另一些人则关注领域知识和外部资源。
• 成功因素的讨论，包括运气、网络和现实中的其他影响，如游说和继承财富。
• 对不同方法论的批评，例如对Lean Startup框架的质疑。

data.article_summary: ClojureCivitas 是一个开放项目，旨在通过创建和分享 Clojure 相关内容来构建知识社区。用户可以轻松贡献内容，无需繁琐设置，只需克隆仓库、创建命名空间、编写代码并提交 pull request。项目强调通过代码内注释捕捉想法和结果，并支持使用表格、图表、markdown 和 hiccup 进行可视化。贡献者可以通过添加 Clojure 命名空间或 markdown 文件来创建文章，并通过 metadata 设置标题、作者、标签等信息。图片也可以添加到命名空间文件夹中，并通过 markdown 显示。完成后，用户提交 pull request，内容经过审核合并后将自动发布到网站。项目还提供实时预览工具，方便用户在编写时查看效果。ClojureCivitas 鼓励开放协作，旨在构建有意义的学习资源网络。

Clojure Civitas
Clojure Civitas makes it easy for you to publish Clojure ideas and explorations
without the overhead of setting up a new project, blog, or repo.
Whether you're sketching out a quick experiment or writing a deeper post,
just fork this repo, create a namespace, write, commit and submit a pull request.
This is your shared scratch space.
Think. Code. Share.
⚡ No setup – Clone this repo, make a new namespace, start coding.
✍️ Write as you code – Capture notes, results, and ideas as you go as comments.
🚀 Easy to share – Create a Pull Request, once merged it appears on the
Clojure Civitas Website
.
🧠 Build shared knowledge – Your work becomes part of a community resource.
🧪 Visualize – Your normal REPL workflow, but with tables, charts, markdown, and hiccup.
Rationale
Why markdown in code? We value reproducible artifacts.
See
Clojure Civitas Rationale
.
Contributing
Exploramus, Communicamus, Crescimus
We explore, we share, we grow.
Your perspective matters.
Pull Requests invited, that's the point!

When using Clay interactively it renders directly to HTML for speed.
Previewing the Website with Quarto
(Optional, Not Recommended)

This will open a browser displaying the site locally.

Publish
Create a pull request:
fork the repository
make changes in a new branch and commit them
push the branch to your fork
open a pull request
Your pull request will be reviewed to prevent abuse and then merged.
Once merged, namespaces are automatically published to the website.

data.title: Welcome to the IPv4 Games
data.author: chillax
data.article_summary: 这篇文章描述了一个名为"IPv4 Turf War"的游戏或活动，参与者可以通过IPv4地址"占领"虚拟土地。活动仅支持IPv4地址，使用IPv6地址的用户无法参与。页面显示了当前顶级玩家、最近的占领记录以及/8区块的领导者。参与者可以查看实时排行和自己的占领情况。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：关于一个游戏的链接以及对IPv4地址相关的讨论

不同观点：
• johnisgood对游戏本身表达了兴趣，表示已经花了一个小时玩这个游戏，并询问该游戏的源代码是否可用。这表明他对游戏的技术实现或开发细节感兴趣。

• nicman23的评论似乎与讨论主线无关，提到“femboy.cat”和“0.2%的互联网”，更像是一种随意的、偏离主题的评论，没有直接回应游戏或IPv4的相关话题。

• chrismorgan提到了一个与IPv4相关的历史讨论，指出“Welcome to the IPv4 Games”这个标题曾经被修改过，原标题是“IPv4 Turf War”，并提供了一个之前讨论的链接（https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=32790429）。这表明chrismorgan关注的是标题的变化和相关讨论的历史。

• snvzz暗示了IPv4地址空间正在被垄断的问题，指出了有人正在大量占用IPv4地址空间，虽然没有具体说明是谁或如何垄断，但表达了对IPv4资源分配的关注。

补充讨论：
• 讨论中出现了偏离主题的评论（nicman23），但整体上围绕两个核心话题：一是关于一个具体游戏的体验及技术细节的兴趣（johnisgood），二是对IPv4地址空间相关问题的关注和历史讨论（chrismorgan和snvzz）。

• IPv4地址垄断的问题是一个潜在的争议点，虽然没有展开详细讨论，但snvzz的评论暗示了对互联网资源分配不均的担忧。

• chrismorgan提供了额外的背景信息，将当前讨论与之前的讨论联系起来，有助于理解标题变化的背景。

data.title: Introduction to Unikernel: Building, deploying lightweight, secure applications
data.author: eyberg
data.article_summary:
这篇文章主要介绍了Unikernel这一独特的应用环境，将其比作私人别墅，强调其独占资源、不与其他应用共享的特性。Unikernel是一种紧凑、专为单一应用设计的虚拟机，能提高速度、效率和安全性。文章解释了传统操作系统如Linux和Windows的局限性，它们因同时运行多个应用而导致资源管理复杂和性能开销大。Unikernel通过将应用与操作系统内核合并成单一可执行映像，减少不必要的功能和服务，从而降低资源消耗和安全风险，并提高执行速度。

文章还讨论了目前较为稳定的两种Unikernel——Nanos和Unikraft，并详细介绍了如何逐步构建和部署Nanos unikernel。通过使用名为OPS的工具，用户可以简化创建和部署过程。Unikernel的优势在于其精简设计带来的更快的启动时间和更低的内存消耗。

不同观点：
• **Unikernels的周期性兴趣**：[perbu]认为Unikernels是一个有趣的概念，但程序员每隔五年就会重新发现一次，就像函数式编程一样，暗示对Unikernels的兴趣可能是周期性且不持久的。

• **NanosVM Inception的技术细节**：[tuananh]对NanosVM Inception的具体工作原理及其包含的内容感到好奇，特别是对AWS市场上的相关产品（链接）表示关注，希望了解更多技术细节。

• **Unikernels的生命力**：[alrs]用“Undead, undead, undead”来形容Unikernels，暗示Unikernels可能是一种看似消亡但实际仍存在或反复出现的技术，对其持续的生命力提出了一种看法。

• **Unikernels在Java框架中的应用**：[wiradikusuma]对Unikernels能否应用于Java框架（如Quarkus或Spring）表示关注，认为这是判断Unikernels实用性的一个重要标志，暗示当前在这些领域的应用可能还不够成熟。

补充讨论：
• 对Unikernels的兴趣周期性和技术成熟度的质疑。
• 对具体技术实现和产品细节的关注。
• 对Unikernels在特定开发框架中应用的期待和质疑。

争议焦点：Unikernels是否能够在主流开发框架（如Java框架）中得到有效应用，以及其长期的技术生命力。

44757249.article_content:
Have you ever wondered what it would be like to have everything in the world just for yourself — where every resource and every service is just for you? Imagine you have rented a private villa on a small, quiet island. Everything in the villa — the rooms, the pool, and the beach — is just for you. No other guests can use anything there, and the staff are there just for you. Isn’t that exciting? I’m sure it is!
This concept also applies to applications, which are given their own space to work in without interference from others and without sharing resources. Any application could thrive in such an environment. So, the question is: “Does such an application environment exist?”
Enter unikernels — a unique application environment that can provide an exclusive environment just like your private villa. They are compact, single-application virtual machines, boosting speed, efficiency, and security.
In this article, we will take a closer look at what unikernels are, explore the different types of unikernels, discuss their benefits and limitations, and learn how to create and deploy a simple Nanos application (a type of unikernel) on AWS.
What is a Unikernel and why do we need it?
Before we look at unikernels, let us first understand why we need something like unikernels in the first place, and examine the limitations of current operating systems like Linux and Windows that lead us to look for alternatives.
Traditional operating systems are designed to run multiple applications simultaneously, which requires careful resource management to ensure smooth operation. The operating system kernel also performs numerous background tasks via memory management, process scheduling, disk I/O and peripheral management. However, our backend applications often do not need these functions, and yet the kernel consumes a lot of memory and CPU power to support them.
The solution to the above problem is simple: if the operating system causes too much overhead, why not let the user-space program take control of the hardware directly? This way, the application essentially becomes part of the kernel, accesses the hardware with fewer obstacles and significantly reduces the overhead of the operating system.
This is exactly the goal of unikernels — fine-tuning for specific tasks. They are lightweight, specialized virtual machines designed to run a single application, making the system smaller, faster and more secure. This unique form of virtualization merges the application and operating system into a single executable image, eliminating the need for the extensive features and services of traditional operating systems.
This specialization makes the system simpler and reduces resource consumption. It only contains the essential components required for the respective application and is, therefore, much smaller than conventional operating systems. This lean design leads to faster boot times and lower memory consumption. In addition, the smaller attack surface of unikernels also improves security.
Since it is executed as a single process, there is no overhead from context switching between multiple processes, resulting in faster execution and lower latency. Once compiled, unikernels can be run on local devices on Linux with QEMU and even on various hypervisors such as Xen, KVM, Nitro System and ESXi.
These hypervisors handle the interaction with the underlying hardware, allowing unikernels to benefit from virtualization without the overhead of a full operating system. The following block diagram will help you to better understand and visualize the whole thing.
Types of Unikernel
Recently, we reached out to several unikernel teams for one of our projects, but only received a few responses. After investigating some of the unikernels, we realized that only two — Nanos and Unikraft — are on the path to stability. Although conceptually both have the same basic principle, they have their own methods for deploying unikernel images and instances.
The main differences between the two unikernels are listed in the table below. However, one of the main differences between Unikraft and Nanos is that Unikraft relies more on its own cloud structure called Unikraft Cloud (which is ultimately based on a bare metal instance) for better performance, while Nanos offers the ability to create its own image that can run on all instance types on all cloud providers supported by Nanos.
Building Nanos unikernel (step-by-step instructions)
We have mentioned about Unikraft, but let’s leave that aside for now and concentrate on nanos.
Creating a Nanos unikernel involves several steps, from setting up the environment to deploying the final image and instance. In addition, Nanos uses an operational tool called OPS that streamlines various tasks, such as image and instance creation.

data.author: Avshalom
data.article_summary: 文章由语言学家M Corvi撰写，描述了慢性疾病患者在寻求诊断和表达病痛时的困境。作者讲述了自己在多次求医后，虽然进行了各种测试，但始终缺乏明确的诊断或语言来描述自己的症状，如 mast cell activation syndrome (MCAS) 和 postural orthostatic tachycardia syndrome (POTS)。作者指出，医学常依赖可观察的现象，但对如疼痛或不适等主观感受缺乏准确的描述和测量方法。作者强调，患者和医生需合作寻找或发明适当的词汇来表达这些“看不见”的感受，并认为定性描述应先于定量测量，以全面了解疾病。文章呼吁对“无形”疾病如长新冠（Long COVID）进行更深入的理解和研究。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：量化功能障碍和描述慢性病症状的挑战

不同观点：
• PaulKeeble认为Funcap问卷在量化Long Covid和ME/CFS患者的功能残疾方面表现良好，尤其是对PEM（运动后恶化）的测量。尽管问卷在描述疲劳等症状时仍有不足，但它提供了一种精确的方法来衡量病人的虚弱程度。PaulKeeble强调了语言在描述个人感觉方面的局限性，特别是对于没有经历过这些症状的人来说。

• Stared指出，语言使用的个体差异使得像幸福感或疼痛程度等主观体验的量化存在困难。即便如此，经验和其对生活的影响是真实的。他们建议使用LLM（大型语言模型）来处理日常记录，从而更准确地反映个人内部现实，以克服传统问卷的局限性。

• Onecommentman引用了“疑病症”的概念，并讨论了其可能对医疗成本的影响。他提到，一些人会因为学习到人体的各种故障模式而变得疑病，这可能导致不必要的医疗支出。

Commentary
As a linguist, I want to find the words to measure chronic illness
Written by
M Corvi
–
August 1, 2025
Heather Hogan / The Sick Times
Let me paint a scene that is all too familiar: I’m not feeling well (again), I go to the doctor (again), they take some blood (again; I turn my head away) and poke at me in whatever way my insurance company deems appropriate.
The result is a long sheet of seemingly arbitrary numbers that indicate
something
about my metabolic processes and the resulting sensations, and I leave without much information aside from some variation of: “These tests tell me that your body seems to be functioning the way everyone else’s is. So we leave you linguistically empty-handed, without a diagnosis or words for these sensations. In conclusion, you’re fine.”
Then why do I feel like I’m full of noodles and static electricity? Where’s the electric noodle test, Doc?
If you also have a complex chronic illness, you’re probably familiar with this experience. These conditions and diseases create a massive linguistic gap that can be difficult for patients to bridge — and even more difficult for medical providers because they don’t experience what we do every day in our bodies.
So what words can I, a linguist and a patient with sensations perceivable only to me, use to fully capture these
mast cell activation syndrome (MCAS
) and
postural orthostatic tachycardia syndrome (POTS)
sensations to my providers?
And, more generally,
how can we measure
our unsettling internal realities if we can’t even name them? How do you effectively measure something like pain, cognitive dysfunction, or feelings of noodliness when so much of medical measurement is reliant on readily observable phenomena — or, stuff that usually has really precise words?
In these moments when I am overwhelmed by this gap, I remind myself that
immaterial to others
doesn’t mean
unreal
— and that, after all, people have words to explain immaterial concepts like gods and quantum physics. The words for these unseeable sensations in my body must exist
somewhere
, and it’s up to patients and healthcare providers to work together to either find or invent them.

My body has always been quick to reject the world. With a family full of medical anomalies, I knew I would one day get my own diagnoses. Growing up, I had seen women in my family suffer from things that were readily dismissed by both clinicians and the general public — namely, chronic pain, fibromyalgia, and migraines. There was never a doubt in my mind that these illnesses caused suffering in the bodies of the people I cared about, even if I couldn’t see or feel the sensations that characterize them.
Eventually, many of these sensations would manifest in my own body. They are bizarre, uncomfortable, and painful sensations that I frequently struggle to find the words for.
I suspected I had MCAS in spring 2019. I began to react strangely to food I’d enjoyed my entire life, had sudden bouts of unexplainable hives, and was often dizzy. To advocate for myself with doctors, I consulted the much-hated “Dr. Google” (that’s
Dr. Google Scholar
to you!). I read any peer-reviewed paper with the right keywords, Wikipedia’d the hell out of any biology I didn’t know, frequented message board after message board, and eventually cobbled together a list of the appropriate tests for my symptoms.
I knew something was wrong with me, and I was determined to articulate it into numerical existence. I eventually did get my diagnosis in March 2022 — which is, comparatively speaking, a very short timeline for receiving a diagnosis of MCAS. I was diagnosed with POTS a few months later after going through a similar gauntlet.
I knew something was wrong with me, and I was determined to articulate it into numerical existence.
Over the course of my diagnoses and ongoing treatment, I’ve internalized a few things about language, illness, and measurement. The first is that, even though it gets easier over time, how I describe the sensations in my body will always be inadequate. That’s not a reflection of me — language can express only so much, and I can’t AirDrop my sensations to another human to make them feel exactly what I’m feeling.
Second, my doctors and I can’t just take a yardstick or thermometer to sensations like pain or discomfort to measure them. Before measuring these sensations in a quantitative, or numerical, way (e.g., a person may be 62 inches tall), we first need a qualitative, or descriptive (e.g. an apple may be green) understanding of what is going on. To get the fullest picture of illness, we need to account for both the quantitative and qualitative — and the qualitative work will always inform the quantitative work.

data.title: Trust in AI coding tools is plummeting
data.author: kiyanwang
data.article_summary: 根据Stack Overflow 2025年开发者调查，开发者对AI编码工具的信任和依赖显著下降。信任AI输出准确性的开发者比例从2024年的43%降至33%，而愿意将AI工具纳入工作流的开发者比例从72%降至60%。尽管84%的开发者使用或计划使用AI工具，但对其满意度明显降低。专家认为，这种转变源于开发者对AI能力与局限有了更现实的认识，不再盲目信任。许多开发者发现AI在处理已知任务时表现不佳，导致信任度下降。不过，调查也显示开发者正更谨慎地使用AI工具，理解其适用场景，以提高生产力，而非完全放弃。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：AI工具的有效性、局限性以及其在实际开发中的影响

不同观点：
• [rkozik1989] 认为AI工具采用暴力方法解决问题，缺乏工程师的潜意识思维，因此即使解决了问题，往往也不是最佳方案。他还指出，AI在发现问题上的能力有限，更多依赖于用户反馈，并对一些CEO过度宣传AI的未来表示怀疑，认为至少还需要10年才能实现他们所承诺的理想未来。

• [fardinahsan] 指出StackOverflow的用户正在流失到AI工具，因此剩下的用户对AI持怀疑态度可能是偏见。他个人已经不再使用StackOverflow。

• [yakattak] 认为当前AI正进入Gartner hype cycle中的"失望之谷"，但这反而是迈向"生产力高原"的必要阶段。他通过个人经验说明，LLM在处理具体任务时表现良好，但如果让其自主运行，使用者对代码的理解会迅速下降。

• [mutkach] 提供了一个StackOverflow的AI调查链接，可能暗示调查数据能提供更多关于AI工具使用情况的见解。

• [odinellefsen] 提到AI工具正变得越来越昂贵。

• [hollownobody] 讽刺性地评论，认为那些抱怨AI工具不好的公司实际上是因为受到AI工具的影响最大，暗示这些公司对AI工具有依赖性。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点在于AI工具是否如一些CEO所宣传的那样能够迅速改变产品开发周期，以及AI工具在实际应用中是否真正有效和经济。
• 讨论还涉及AI工具对开发者社区的影响，如StackOverflow用户流失和AI使用成本上升的问题。
• Gartner hype cycle被引用来说明AI技术发展所处的阶段，预示着未来可能的生产力提升。

Trust in AI coding tools is plummeting
According to Stack Overflow's 2025 developer survey.
By
Chris Stokel-Walker
August 04, 2025
You have
1
article left to read this month before you need to
register
a free LeadDev.com account.
A new Stack Overflow survey highlights a steep decline in trust and reliance on AI coding tools, as users get more discerning.
Stack Overflow’s
annual survey of nearly 50,000 developers
acts as a useful benchmark of how software engineers are feeling, and this year’s results suggest a steep decline in sentiment around
AI coding tools
.
This year, 33% of developers said they trust the accuracy of the outputs they receive from AI tools, down from 43% in 2024. At the same time, how favourably developers think of adding AI tools into their workflow fell steeply, from 72% in 2024 to 60% this year.
The 10-plus percentage point swing in both questions was something that stood out to the team behind the survey, too. “One of the most notable trends in this year’s survey is the continued rise in AI tool usage – now at 84% of developers using or planning to use them – contrasted with a clear drop in favourability,” says Erin Yepis, senior analyst for market research and insights at
Stack Overflow
.

(Required)

This field is for validation purposes and should be left unchanged.
What’s behind the shift?
Yepis says there are “likely a few forces at play here.” She points out that there was a
gap between the perception of satisfaction
between simple, everyday tasks that devs might do often, and those that they don’t.
“When AI is used for general tasks by those that know what they are looking for, there is not only less room to increase satisfaction, but those tools immediately create a poor experience, too,” she says.
The underwhelming performance of AI at things developers already know how to do is just one indication of why there has been a shift in sentiment. “Developer trust in AI is becoming more realistic as the industry moves beyond the initial hype phase. With increased experience, developers now have a better understanding of AI’s capabilities and limitations,” says Raj Kesarapalli, director at application security company Black Duck.
Kesarapalli says that we might be at that inflection point where developers are starting to utilize AI tools more judiciously, and are similarly considering the way they perform when set to the tasks they’re given. “Ultimately, effective use of AI depends on understanding its strengths and weaknesses and knowing when and how to leverage it,” he says.
More like this
The programming languages facing an AI-driven existential crisis
Kari McMahon
11 generative AI programming tools for developers
Harry Guinness
Hype versus reality
The reality of performance versus hype is why Andrey Korchak, a longtime former chief technology officer, believes we are seeing plummeting trust figures in Stack Overflow’s survey.
“One of the most common stories I hear in 2025 goes like this: someone gives an AI coding agent a try, expecting magic,” he says. “But after a few actions, it messes up the architecture, changes something it shouldn’t, or just spits out bad code.”
At that point, Korchak says, many people might step away from AI, without realizing that the time invested can pay dividends through better prompts or more reasonable expectations.
The answer, for now, is more human oversight of AI outputs to understand
why
AI tools are failing to carry out user requests as intended. Three in four developers who responded to Stack Overflow’s survey say they’ll revert to human oversight when they don’t trust an AI-generated answer.
But there is still a silver lining, says Yepis. “It’s not that developers are abandoning AI – usage is growing, and 69% of the developers using
AI agents
at work agree that productivity is improving,” she says.
Instead, the stats show that developers are using AI more judiciously. “They’re learning
where AI fits in their workflows
– and where it doesn’t,” she says. “That’s a natural progression as a new technology matures: initial enthusiasm gives way to realism, and we’re seeing that shift play out in this year’s results.”

A gentle introduction to DSPy for graph data enrichment
Prashanth Rao
AI Engineer at Kùzu Inc.
Aug 4, 2025
example
Constructing real-world knowledge graphs often involves combining or merging data from multiple sources.
However, the same entity may be represented in different ways across these sources, leading to challenges
in disambiguating similar-looking entities that we can merge into a unified dataset.
If you’ve ever faced this kind of problem when working with graphs or data in general,
you’ve come to the right place!
In this post, we’ll showcase a two-part workflow involving vector embeddings and an “LLM-as-a-judge”
to disambiguate entities so that we can enrich one dataset with information from another. The LLM
part of the workflow uses
DSPy
, a declarative framework for building
compound AI pipelines. The goal of this post is to give a gentle introduction to DSPy and the powerful
primitives it provides, so that you can repurpose these ideas and be more productive applying
LLMs in your own domains.
Motivation
Graphs are a powerful way to represent complex relationships between entities — finding
centres of influence within a network can yield valuable insights in numerous domains. A particularly
interesting graph that we’ll use in this post, is the Nobel laureate mentorship network, which captures
the professor-student relationships of Nobel laureates and candidates (termed “scholars”).

graph question

interconnected mentorship relations

a Nobel prize, or “scholar” if they did not), and category and year of the award (if applicable).

data.author: lurkshark
data.article_summary: CNN调查披露，朝鲜政权利用AI和美国脆弱群体，通过伪装成美国求职者渗透美国公司，赚取数百万美元资助军事项目。朝鲜IT人员使用假身份和AI技术，如简历生成和面部伪装软件，隐藏真实身份，在视频面试中冒充西方开发人员和工程师。美国内部的协助者帮助他们获取笔记本电脑和访问金融系统，使他们能远程工作并绕过国际制裁。专家估计，数千名朝鲜IT人员已 infiltrated 美国企业，甚至涉及财富500强公司。美国司法部警告，这不仅违反制裁，还威胁国家安全。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：远程工作（WFH）与办公室工作（RTO）的优缺点，以及远程工作可能引发的安全问题（如诈骗）。

不同观点：
• **对远程工作的保留态度**：用户"quantified"表示不喜欢回归办公室工作（RTO），因为通勤在远程工作（WFH）中有明显改善。然而，他们承认远程员工可能更容易执行一些复杂的骗局，尤其是那些可能产生重大影响的骗局。这表明他们对远程工作持部分保留态度，关注其潜在的安全隐患。

• **对远程工作潜在问题的关注**：虽然"quantified"没有完全否定远程工作，但他们特别提到了远程员工有能力执行“更有趣的骗局”，暗示远程工作环境可能让某些类型的欺诈行为更加容易实施。这显示出对远程工作在安全和监管方面的担忧。

补充讨论：
• **推荐相关资源**：用户"e40"没有直接讨论远程工作或办公室工作的优劣，而是通过推荐BBC的播客《The Lazarus Heist》将讨论引向远程工作可能涉及的复杂骗局问题。该用户强调了该播客提供了大量相关细节，并高度推荐。此外，他们还对CNN的一篇文章表示赞赏，认为CNN在网络开发方面有所提升，这可能暗示对相关媒体报道质量的认可。

争议焦点：
• 远程工作虽然提供了诸如免通勤等优势，但其在安全和监管方面可能存在漏洞，尤其是在涉及复杂骗局和网络安全问题时。这可能是评论中隐含的争议点，即如何在享受远程工作优势的同时，确保工作环境的安全和合规性。

总结来看，评论中的主要讨论围绕远程工作的优缺点展开，其中特别关注了远程工作可能带来的安全隐患，如复杂的骗局和欺诈行为。同时，有用户提供了相关资源以深入了解这些问题。

• 观点一：Frieren认为微软和整个科技行业应将安全性视为一个基本的支柱，而不是事后才考虑。这表明目前的科技公司在追求利润的同时忽视了安全问题，用户需要主动检查设置并要求公司承担责任。论据包括用户自我保护的必要性和公司目前对安全性不够重视的现状。

• 观点二：Frieren指出，单靠用户无法改变微软等大公司的行为，必须通过政府法规和法律来强制执行安全标准。他认为严格的法规和具备强制执行力的法律才能迫使大公司关注安全性。这里的论据是投资者只关心公司股价，不关心安全性，因为安全问题不会直接影响他们的利益。

• 观点三：Frieren提到，自己无法单独改变微软，但可以通过投票支持能够推动这种改变的政府。这表明他对政治手段和政府干预抱有希望，认为这是实现科技公司安全改革的有效途径。

补充讨论：
• 评论中隐含了对科技公司逐利本质的批评，特别是在安全性与利润发生冲突时，公司倾向于选择后者。
• 强调了用户在当前环境下的无力感，认为个体用户难以对大公司施加足够的压力，必须依靠集体行动和政府干预。
• 争议焦点在于如何有效推动科技公司加强安全性，是通过用户自我保护和市场压力，还是依赖政府法规和法律强制执行。

data.title: So you want to parse a PDF?
data.author: UglyToad
data.article_summary: 本文介绍了解析PDF文件的过程及其面临的挑战。理想情况下，解析PDF包括以下步骤：找到文件头、定位交叉引用表指针、查找所有对象偏移量，以及构建指向目录字典的尾部字典。PDF文件由对象组成，对象包含内容并可以通过间接引用来参考其他对象。为了避免扫描整个文件，PDF使用交叉引用表（xref）来索引对象位置。理论上，文件末尾有指向xref的指针，但现实中格式混乱，如标记位置不准确或拼写错误。此外，一些文件可能包含多个xref表或流，且某些文件的PDF内容起始偏移量非零，导致解析困难。对随机抽取的3977个文件的分析显示，约0.5%的文件存在xref声明错误，使得解析过程更加复杂。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：PDF解析的复杂性及其解决方案

不同观点：
• **diptanu**：认为计算机视觉方法（如将PDF转换为图像并进行布局分析）在处理多种来源的PDF时效果更好，因为依赖元数据的方法无法扩展。其公司开发的API正是基于这种方法，通过多个模型组合来实现高准确度。
• **gcanyon**：提出一个理想化的解决方案，即所有生成PDF的应用都应附加统一的机器友好元数据，以便于解析。然而，现实中如其名字被错误解析的例子表明，这并没有被广泛实施。
• **farkin88**：指出增量保存链在多次编辑后可能导致PDF解析问题，许多现实世界中的文档需要构建类似的修复路径以实现正确解析。
• **userbinator**：认为PDF格式由于混合了文本和二进制数据而非常奇怪，并且较新的PDF版本引入了更复杂的结构（如xref流和对象流），增加了解析难度。
• **mft_**：主张摆脱基于布局的交流方式，建议采用“机器优先”或“内容优先”的格式（如JSON、XML），以简化程序化处理和数据提取。

补充讨论：
• **jupin**和**leeter**：以幽默和实际经历表达了对PDF解析困难的无奈，将其比喻为“PDF地狱”和“混沌”。
• **simonw**：支持使用OCR和视觉LLM处理复杂布局的PDF，并指出一些LLM已经支持这种方法。
• **HocusLocus**：提到PDF的Postscript形式和压缩算法，并建议通过解析和重排对象来处理PDF，同时对Gemini不支持EPUB表示遗憾。
• **sychou**：认为PDF和HTML/CSS/JS是解析和显示中的两大挑战，消耗了大量AI计算资源。
• **ccgreg**：提供了一个包含8百万PDF文件的数据集链接，供研究和解析使用。

争议焦点：
• PDF解析的理想解决方案与现实应用之间的差距。理想中通过统一元数据可以简化解析，但现实中由于各种应用生成的PDF格式不规范，导致依赖元数据的方法不可行。
• 计算机视觉方法与传统元数据解析方法的优劣对比，前者在处理复杂和不规范PDF时表现出更好的鲁棒性。

44780353.article_content:
So you want to parse a PDF?
03 Aug, 2025
Suppose you have an appetite for tilting at windmills. Let's say you love pain. Well then why not write a PDF parser today?
The ideal world: how the specification should work
Conceptually parsing a PDF is fairly simple:
First, locate the version header comment at the start of the file
Next you need to locate the pointer to the cross-reference
Then you can find all object offsets
Finally you locate and build the trailer dictionary which points to the catalog dicitionary
Introduction to PDF objects
A PDF object wraps some valid PDF content, numbers, strings, dictionaries, etc., in an object and generation number. The content is surrounded by the
obj/endobj
markers, for example a simple number may have its own PDF object:
16 0 obj
620
endobj
This declares that object 16 with generation 0 contains the number 620.
A PDF file is effectively a graph of objects that may reference each other. Objects reference other objects by use of indirect references. These have the format "16 0 R" which indicates that the content
should be found in object 16 (generation number 0). In this case that would point to the object 16 containing the number 620. It is up to producer applications to split file content into objects as they wish, though the specification requires that certain object types be indirect.
Finding the cross-reference offset
To avoid the need to scan the entire file, PDFs declare a cross-reference table (xref). This is an index pointing to where each object in the file lives.
Each file ends with a pointer to the cross-reference file:
<< %trailer >>
startxref
116
%%EOF
This tells the parser to jump to byte offset 116 to find the xref table (or stream). In theory this pointer is right at the end of the file, according to the specification:
Applications should read a PDF file from its end. The last line of the file contains only the end-of-file marker,
%%EOF
Though the specification says the
%%EOF
marker should be on the last line, in practice, things are much messier. For example, Adobe Acrobat only requires it to be within the last 1024 bytes. In real files it can appear anywhere.
In addition files encountered in the wild lacked a linebreak before the offset declaration, or had a typo, e.g.
startref
.
Let's assume you're able to find the declared cross-reference offset for now.
Finding all object offsets
At the specified offset you should find a well-formatted xref table:
xref
7 4
0000000000 65535 f
0000109882 00000 n
0000109933 00000 n
0000140066 00000 n
After the
xref
indicator appears, followed by a line break, the first object number and count of objects in the subsection are given. This means: start at object 7 and list 4 objects. Each line gives the byte offset, generation number, and status (n for in-use, f for free). From this, we know where to find objects 8-10 in the file.
So in the example above -- skipping the free entry for object 7 -- this xref table tells where to find the following objects:
Object 8 (generation 0) at offset 109882
Object 9 (generation 0) at offset 109933
Object 10 (generation 0) at offset 140066
Note: files can have multiple xref tables or streams, linked by
/Prev
entries in their trailers.
Locating the trailer dictionary
Finally, above the startxref marker, you'll find the trailer dictionary. This provides key metadata, most importantly, where to find the root object. Once you have that, you can follow references and begin interpreting the content.
The real world: where your pain begins
Assuming everything is well behaved and you have a reasonable parser for PDF objects this is fairly simple. But you cannot assume everything is well behaved. That would be very foolish, foolish indeed. You're in PDF hell
now. PDF isn't a specification, it's a social construct, it's a vibe. The more you struggle the deeper you sink. You live in the bog now, with the rest of us, far from the sight of God. If your parser expects files to obey the specification it will fail and people will think it is broken and pitiable. They will think that you are very silly.
The challenges of locating the xref pointer
We've already mentioned a few unexpected ways locating the pointer to the first cross-reference can fail:
It is not at the end of the file, nor within the last 1024 bytes of the file.
It is misspelled.
It is not in the format you'd expect.
But assuming you find a pointer, that's where the real fun begins. Because the pointer is not your friend, it is the first lie, you don't appreciate how deep the rabbit hole goes.
In screening 3977 files taken from the
common crawl corpus
at random we detected 23 files with a bad xref declaration. This works out to a roughly 0.5% failure rate in the sample set.
PDF content starting at a non-zero offset
In these files the
startxref
pointer is incorrect due to a non-zero PDF content start.
This happens when there's junk data before the
%PDF-
version header. This shifts every single byte offset in the file.

data.title: Writing a good design document
data.author: kiyanwang
data.article_summary: 这篇文章介绍了如何撰写优秀的设计文档。设计文档类似于数学证明，旨在说服读者该设计在给定条件下是最优的，最重要的是要说服作者自己。撰写过程帮助理清模糊的直觉，揭示思维的漏洞。良好的文档组织和代码组织一样重要，避免写出“意大利面条式文档”。文档应清晰流畅，避免让读者感到意外，每句话都应自然衔接。编辑时应尽量简化，删除不必要的词语，以节省读者注意力。多加练习是关键，通过批改他人文档和精简自己的表达可以提高写作能力。文章还提供了一些具体建议，如使用短段落和将文档视作一系列相互衔接的要点。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：技术设计文档的结构和重要性

不同观点：
• **nickm12** 认为技术设计文档应像洋葱一样分为三层：问题陈述、目标和需求，功能规范，以及技术规范。每个部分应相互衔接，且如果某一节存在致命缺陷，则无需继续阅读。文档的目的是充分解决问题，而不是追求最优。
• **patrickmay** 强调写作能够提升想法的质量，并引用Leslie Lamport的话来说明写作揭示思维的混乱。他认为设计文档至关重要，并对技术写作质量的提升提供了建议，如参考"Write Like an Amazonian"。
• **B-Con** 强调设计文档应简化复杂内容，不应包含过多的智力挣扎和错误的开始。这些内容可以放在附录中，但主文档应保持简单易懂。
• **farkin88** 指出设计文档批准后的维护问题，并建议使用轻量级的架构决策记录（ADRs）来解决文档随时间衰减的问题。
• **mtlynch** 对Amazon的会议模式提出质疑，认为让所有人在会议上同步阅读文档是浪费时间，并建议在会前阅读文档以提高会议效率。
• **chartered_stack** 强调了具体示例对理解良好设计文档的重要性，并询问是否有公开的示例可供学习。
• **cadamsdotcom** 提供了一种利用LLM（大语言模型）来组织和简化文档写作过程的方法，强调文档的反复修改和简化。
• **lastdong** 通过技术写作课程提高了总结文档的能力，强调使用尽可能少的文字来清晰传达概念，并指出这是一种需要定期训练的技能。
• **norseboar** 认为并非所有读者都愿意跟随作者的推理过程，有些读者只想知道结论。因此，文档应根据读者需求调整写作方式。
• **nrvn** 分享了创建RFC模板的经验，并建议根据组织的大小和需求调整模板结构，而不是盲目模仿。
• **metadat** 对文章的空泛和缺乏有效示例表示失望，并指出 cargo-cult 内容常常获得过多关注，导致一些奇怪的结果。
• **ryanmadden** 认为组织和清晰度是软件工程师提高文档写作的最大障碍，并分享了自己在谷歌的经验和写作心得。
• **kator** 分享了在Amazon工作的经验，强调从客户需求出发撰写设计文档。
• **matt-p** 指出有时设计文档可能只为自己阅读，但仍认为写下来非常有帮助，并请求示例文档以进行比较。

补充讨论：
• 技术设计文档的结构和层次：包括问题陈述、目标、需求、功能规范、技术规范等部分的必要性和顺序。
• 文档的写作和编辑过程：包括利用LLM、反复修改、简化文字等方法。
• 文档的阅读和会议讨论方式：包括会前阅读文档、同步阅读的效率问题等。
• 文档的维护和后续记录：包括使用ADRs等方法解决文档随时间衰减的问题。
• 具体示例的需求：多位参与者提到需要公开的示例文档来帮助理解和学习。

争议焦点：
• 文档是否应包含详细的推理过程还是直接给出结论：nickm12和norseboar的观点在此存在分歧。
• 会议中同步阅读文档的效率问题：mtlynch和传统Amazon会议模式的争议。
• 文档写作的最佳实践和示例需求：多个参与者提到需要具体示例来更好地理解和应用所学知识。

44779428.article_content:
How to write a good design document
This essay is a version of
the response
I gave to my friend Vik's call for suggestions:
had a lot of people ask how they can learn to write design docs, and i didn’t have a good answer besides “work at a place with writing culture and smart senior engineers”. anyone have more useful advice?
https://t.co/7F9BV31shv
— vik (@vikhyatk)
August 31, 2024
Definition
A design document is a technical report that outlines the implementation strategy of a system in the context of trade-offs and constraints.
Goal
Think of a design document like a proof in mathematics. The goal of a proof is to convince the reader that the theorem is true. The goal of a design document is to convince the reader the design is optimal given the situation.
The most important person to convince is
the author
. The act of writing a design document helps to add rigor to what are otherwise vague intuitions. Writing reveals how sloppy your thinking was (and later, code will show how sloppy your writing was).
Organization
Good design document organization is as important as code organization. You probably have opinions about code organization. You've probably used the phrase "spaghetti code" to describe poorly-organized code. Most programmers write "spaghetti design docs" unless they've had a lot of practice.
Let me illustrate a common code organization issue some programmers run into on their first day. The novice writes
terminal.print("Hello world")
Then they decide they want to make the text red, so they edit their program to
terminal.print("Hello world")
terminal.setPrintColor("red")
And then they're confused that it didn't come out red. They haven't internalized that the first line of code
happens before
the second. They just get a soup of code on the screen that kind of has the ingredients for a program, and expect the computer to do what they want.
Novice document writers make the
exact
same mistake, but with prose instead of code. They get a soup of sentences and paragraphs and expect the reader's brain to do what they want.
If the reader is smart enough, you might actually get away with this. Just like an expert programmer can mentally untangle spaghetti code.
But a perfect doc is written such that the reader
is never surprised
. The reader should find that every sentence flows obviously from the previous ones. They should finish your doc and think "well this was entirely straightforward, why did we even need to have this meeting?".
This disappoints the ego-seeking behavior of many engineers. Good engineers often want people to realize how clever they were.
But a good doc will lay out the problem and mental models in a way that the solution that took weeks of hard thought to invent will be clear to the reader by the time the doc presents it.
This also requires having a good model of the minds of the people reading your doc. The goal of your doc is to take their minds from their current state to a new state in which they believe your design is a good one.
You should anticipate every objection someone would have and preemptively show why it's invalid, so that the reader never even thinks to bring it up.
Many engineers fail at modeling the starting state of their readers' minds, so fail at getting them to the destination state.
Editing
Once you've got the information organized and laid out properly, the next step is to edit for length. Remove every word that can be removed. Do this because your readers' attention is a scarce resource.
Unless you're an unusually terse writer, you can almost always cut length by ~30% from the first draft without sacrificing information.
The easiest way to get good at editing by going through
other
people's docs with a red pen and crossing out unnecessary words. You'll find tons. It's easier to criticize other people.
Once you've built this muscle, you can turn the weapon on yourself. Distilling thoughts to fit into the 280 character tweet limit is also surprisingly good practice.
Volume
There's no substitute for lots of practice. I'm grateful for having worked at AWS with a unique doc-writing culture. The first docs I wrote there were terrible, but after a few hundred, I like to think they were pretty good.
For unfamiliar readers: Amazon meetings start with the presenter passing out copies (historically physical, though increasingly digital since Covid) of a prose document. The document is 1-6 pages depending on the importance.
The meeting starts with everyone sitting in silence, reading the document, and adding notes and questions in the margins with red pen. Watching people mark up the document you spent so much time polishing is a
strong
forcing function to become a better writer.
Concrete tips
These work for me, but they may not work for you.
Use short paragraphs
You should think of your doc as a series of bullet points that flow into each other. That is, a doc might be organized like:
Observation A
Observation B
Because B, idea C
But problems D and E
Observation F
Ther

• **patrickmay** 强调写作能够提升想法的质量，并引用Leslie Lamport的话来说明写作揭示思维的混乱。他认为设计文档至关重要，并对技术写作质量的提升提供了建议，如参考"Write Like an Amazonian"。
• **B-Con** 强调设计文档应简化复杂内容，不应包含过多的智力挣扎和错误的开始。这些内容可以放在附录中，但主文档应保持简单易懂。
• **farkin88** 指出设计文档批准后的维护问题，并建议使用轻量级的架构决策记录（ADRs）来解决文档随时间衰减的问题。
• **mtlynch** 对Amazon的会议模式提出质疑，认为让所有人在会议上同步阅读文档是浪费时间，并建议在会前阅读文档以提高会议效率。
• **chartered_stack** 强调了具体示例对理解良好设计文档的重要性，并询问是否有公开的示例可供学习。
• **cadamsdotcom** 提供了一种利用LLM（大语言模型）来组织和简化文档写作过程的方法，强调文档的反复修改和简化。
• **lastdong** 通过技术写作课程提高了总结文档的能力，强调使用尽可能少的文字来清晰传达概念，并指出这是一种需要定期训练的技能。
• **norseboar** 认为并非所有读者都愿意跟随作者的推理过程，有些读者只想知道结论。因此，文档应根据读者需求调整写作方式。
• **nrvn** 分享了创建RFC模板的经验，并建议根据组织的大小和需求调整模板结构，而不是盲目模仿。
• **metadat** 对文章的空泛和缺乏有效示例表示失望，并指出 cargo-cult 内容常常获得过多关注，导致一些奇怪的结果。
• **ryanmadden** 认为组织和清晰度是软件工程师提高文档写作的最大障碍，并分享了自己在谷歌的经验和写作心得。
• **kator** 分享了在Amazon工作的经验，强调从客户需求出发撰写设计文档。
• **matt-p** 指出有时设计文档可能只为自己阅读，但仍认为写下来非常有帮助，并请求示例文档以进行比较。

补充讨论：
• 技术设计文档的结构和层次：包括问题陈述、目标、需求、功能规范、技术规范等部分的必要性和顺序。
• 文档的写作和编辑过程：包括利用LLM、反复修改、简化文字等方法。
• 文档的阅读和会议讨论方式：包括会前阅读文档、同步阅读的效率问题等。
• 文档的维护和后续记录：包括使用ADRs等方法解决文档随时间衰减的问题。
• 具体示例的需求：多位参与者提到需要公开的示例文档来帮助理解和学习。

争议焦点：
• 文档是否应包含详细的推理过程还是直接给出结论：nickm12和norseboar的观点在此存在分歧。
• 会议中同步阅读文档的效率问题：mtlynch和传统Amazon会议模式的争议。
• 文档写作的最佳实践和示例需求：多个参与者提到需要具体示例来更好地理解和应用所学知识。

data.title: Build Your Own Lisp
data.author: lemonberry
data.article_summary: 《Build Your Own Lisp》是一本教你使用C语言创建自己的编程语言的书。全书通过1000行代码，引导读者学习C语言并开发一个类似Lisp的语言。书中探讨了Lisp的独特之处，帮助读者提高实际项目开发能力和问题解决技巧，同时写出优雅的代码。该书提供免费在线阅读，也可购买印刷版或电子书以获得更好的阅读体验。许多读者表示，实现自己的Lisp让他们感到成为更完整的C程序员，并认为每个程序员都应尝试这类项目。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：围绕“构建自己的Lisp”教程的实用性、教育价值以及其局限性的讨论

不同观点：
• cardanome认为该教程不适合用于构建可扩展的Lisp，只是一个玩具语言的实现，长期来看可能传授一些会限制开发者进步的知识。
• tnlogy分享了自己的一个简化版Scheme到C的编译器，并提到该项目是受SICP一书启发，同时质疑SICP是否仍在课程中使用。
• lskfiep指出该教程不仅仅是一个“构建自己的Lisp”教程，更是一个学习C语言和编程语言设计的优秀资源，并强调该教程使用了自定义的解析库'mpc'，虽然缺少一些经典Lisp特性如'car'和'cdr'。
• golly_ned询问是否有使用现代C++编写的类似教程或指南。
• coderatlarge对作者免费提供教程表示感谢，并分享了自己类似的经历，认为通过构建简化版Lisp学习效果更佳，同时强调了测试框架的重要性。
• nyrikki提到过去使用纯Lisp和C的结合学习语言，认为即使是300行的REXX代码也能达到学习效果。
• intellectronica以幽默的方式提出可以让AI来完成构建Lisp的任务。
• dark-star认为大多数此类教程在涉及有趣和高级的主题（如尾调用优化、延续、CPS、call/CC）时就停止了，认为仅构建玩具语言是一个值得称赞的目标。
• ale认为在讨论构建编程语言的教程中，使用Grace Hopper的画像比Ada Lovelace更合适。

补充讨论：
• 争议的焦点在于该教程是否能够有效地帮助学习者构建一个可扩展的Lisp语言，以及其在教学上的价值。
• 讨论中提到了SICP一书的影响力和使用情况，以及现代语言和工具（如C++和AI）在构建Lisp中的应用。
• 还提到了教程中缺少一些经典Lisp特性，以及高级主题（如尾调用优化和延续）的缺失。
• 最后，对教程中使用历史人物画像的适当性提出了不同的看法。

data.title: A Carnival Attraction That Saved Premature Babies (2016)
data.author: pr337h4m
data.article_summary: Martin Couney was a renowned figure who ran infant incubator exhibits for over 30 years, most famously at Coney Island. His displays of premature babies in incubators drew large crowds, with an exhibit at the 1933-1934 Chicago World’s Fair being particularly successful. Couney, alongside pediatrician Dr. Julius Hess, cared for premature babies using advanced incubators, despite controversy over the ethics of displaying the infants. Couney claimed to have studied medicine in Europe, but evidence suggests he never officially qualified as a doctor. Despite this, his work saved thousands of babies and influenced American neonatal medicine, eventually gaining recognition as pioneering, though his lack of formal medical credentials remained a point of contention. His collaboration with Hess marked a significant step in gaining legitimacy in the medical field.

44770215.article_content:
Martin Couney holds up Beth Allen, a premature baby who was on view at the Coney Island attraction.
Beth Allen
Nurses in starched white uniforms and doctors in medical coats tended to babies in glass and steel incubators. The infants had been born many weeks premature and well below a healthy birth weight. Stores didn’t make clothes small enough to fit their tiny, skeletal frames so the nurses dressed them in dolls’ clothes and knitted bonnets.
A sign above the entrance read “Living Babies in Incubators” in letters so large they could be read from the other end of the Chicago World’s Fair grounds, which took place over 18 months in 1933 and 1934. The infant incubator exhibit was built at a cost of $75,000 (worth $1.4 million today) and was painted in a patriotic red, white and blue.
The men in charge were leading Chicago pediatrician Dr. Julius Hess and Martin Couney, who was known across America as “the incubator doctor.” Couney was a lugubrious man in his 60s, with thinning gray hair, a mustache and a stoop, something he jokingly attributed to a lifetime of bending over babies. Couney and Hess employed a team of six nurses and two wet nurses.
Martin Couney had run infant incubator exhibits, in which premature babies were displayed to the public, for more than three decades, most famously at Coney Island in New York City. He had long been regarded by desperate parents as a savior, one who offered medical help to babies written off as “weaklings” by mainstream medicine.
But for Hess, who was accustomed to carrying out his work in a more conventional hospital setting, this was a career first.
Miracle at Coney Island: How a Sideshow Doctor Saved Thousands of Babies and Transformed American Medicine (Kindle Single)
More about this product
The exhibit was a hit with the Chicago public who paid 25 cents and flocked by the hundreds of thousands to see the babies.
To celebrate the success of their facility, Couney organized a “Homecoming” celebration on July 25, 1934, for babies who had “graduated” from the incubators at the Chicago’s World’s Fair the previous summer. Of the 58 babies Couney and Hess had cared for in 1933, 41 returned with their mothers for the reunion. The event was broadcast live on local radio and across the fairgrounds.
On the radio program, Couney’s exhibit was portrayed by the announcer not as a frivolous sideshow spectacle, but as an invaluable medical facility:
The Incubator station for premature babies…is not primarily a place of exhibiting tiny infants. Instead, it is actually a lifesaving station, where prematurely born babies are brought from leading hospitals all over the city, for the care and attention that are afforded. The place is spick and span, with doctors and graduate nurses in constant attendance...
Because of the sideshow setting in which he operated, Couney’s career had always been controversial. Many in the medical professional viewed the “incubator doctor” with suspicion, others with outright hostility. The New York Society for the Prevention of Cruelty to Children had repeatedly accused Couney of exploiting the babies and endangering their lives by putting them on show.
None of the complaints was sustained, and by the 1930s, Couney was finally being taken seriously as a medical pioneer. Couney’s professional collaboration with Hess marked a key stage in his habilitation.
But while doing research for my radio documentary
Life Under Glass
, which is being broadcast on NPR stations around the country this August, and my book,
Miracle at Coney Island
, I made an incredible discovery about a man who has a claim to have changed the course of American neonatal medicine.
Couney never actually qualified as a medical doctor.
Throughout his career, Couney said he had studied medicine in Leipzig and Berlin. However, I could find no evidence of Couney (or Cohn/Cohen as he was known then) having studied medicine at a university in either city. To become a physician in Germany, one was required to write a thesis. The U.S. National Library of Medicine has copies of the German records: the librarians could not locate a thesis written by Couney.
Couney was deliberately evasive about his date and place of birth. I have discovered that he immigrated to the US in 1888 at 19 years old. But someone of that age would not be old enough to have studied at university in Leipzig and Berlin before going on to do graduate work in Paris at the knee of Pierre Budin, the father of European neonatal medicine, as Couney claimed to have done in numerous press interviews.
In the 1910 U.S. census, Couney listed his career as, “surgical instruments.” Though Couney claimed to be the inventor of an incubator, I have been unable to find any evidence that he registered an incubator patent in the U.S. More likely Couney was a technician. Yet by 1930 he was describing himself in the census as a “physician.”

data.title: C10kday
data.author: LorenDB
data.article_summary: 文章宣布2025年8月5日是cURL项目发布以来的第10,000天，称为"c10kday"。为了庆祝这一时刻，项目团队邀请用户分享与cURL相关的故事，包括首次使用cURL的经历、cURL如何帮助解决问题的实例以及它对个人工作或生活的意义。这些故事将在cURL的GitHub讨论区收集和分享，虽然团队在持续开发新功能和修复漏洞，但这个日子依然是与社区互动并回顾美好记忆的契机。最后，文章感谢用户对cURL的支持。

data.title: Apache ECharts 6
data.author: makepanic
data.article_summary:
Apache ECharts 6.0 发布了12项重大升级，旨在提升数据可视化的专业性和灵活性。主要改进围绕三个核心维度：

1. **更专业的视觉表现**：
   - 全新默认主题，现代设计语言。
   - 动态主题切换，无需重新初始化图表。
   - 支持暗黑模式，自动适配系统主题。

2. **扩展数据表达边界**：
   - 新增和弦图、蜂群图、散点抖动、断轴等新图表和功能，处理复杂数据场景。
   - 增强股票交易图表，提升标签能力和开箱即用的图表类型。

3. **释放组合自由**：
   - 新的矩阵坐标系，支持像表格一样组合图表和组件。
   - 增强的自定义系列，支持npm发布和动态注册。
   - 新增小提琴图、轮廓图等自定义图表。
   - 优化轴标签布局，防止重叠。

这些升级使ECharts 6.0在数据可视化方面更加强大、可靠和灵活，帮助开发者创造出更具创意的视觉作品。

44794926.article_content:
Apache ECharts 6 New Features
Twelve years ago, ECharts was first released on GitHub, planting the seed for an open-source journey.
From a simple charting tool to a visualization powerhouse supporting millions of developers; from a single front-end charting library to a comprehensive technology system covering mobile, large screens, and server-side rendering—over these 12 years, we've witnessed ECharts' continuous technical breakthroughs and have been delighted to see developers worldwide create countless stunning data stories with ECharts.
Now, Apache ECharts 6.0 is officially released, bringing 12 major upgrades to take your data visualization to the next level.
Feature Overview
Twelve years of accumulation, all for more ultimate visual expression. The core strength of Apache ECharts has always come from a deep understanding of developers' real challenges. When defining the direction for 6.0, the question was clear:
How can we make complex data presentation both powerful and elegant?
This drove us to evolve deeply around three core dimensions:
More professional visual presentation
: From a meticulously crafted default theme to intelligent dark mode switching, ensuring charts have a professional look and seamlessly integrate into modern applications.
Expanding the boundaries of data expression
: New chart types and features to handle complex scenarios and enable intuitive expression of deep data.
Unleashing freedom of composition
: From the revolutionary matrix coordinate system to reusable custom series and optimized axis labels—empowering developers to freely compose and turn creativity into unconstrained visual works.
We have made 12 upgrades across these three core dimensions. These are not just simple feature additions, but a solid foundation for building the next generation of data-driven applications. They all point to one goal:
to make ECharts powerful, reliable, and stable in the background, leaving the stage and spotlight for your creative expression.
Below, we introduce these twelve upgrades in detail:
More professional visual presentation
1. Brand New Default Theme
: Modern design language for professional data expression
2. Dynamic Theme Switching
: Seamless runtime theme switching for multi-theme scenarios
3. Dark Mode Support
: Automatically adapts to system dark/light mode for better UX
Expanding the boundaries of data expression
4. New Chord Chart
: Visualize complex relationships and distributions
5. New Beeswarm Chart
: Smartly expand overlapping data points into a honeycomb layout
6. New Scatter Jittering
: Add jitter to scatter plots for better readability of dense data
7. New Broken Axis
: Easily present data with large magnitude differences
8. Enhanced Stock Trading Charts
: Improved label capabilities and more out-of-the-box trading charts
Unleashing freedom of composition
9. New Matrix Coordinate System
: Freely combine chart types and components like a table
10. Enhanced Custom Series
: Support npm publishing and dynamic registration for code reuse
11. New Custom Charts
: Violin, contour, stage, bar range, and line range charts
12. Axis Label Optimization
: Smarter default axis label layout to prevent overflow and overlap
With these upgrades, Apache ECharts 6.0 helps users create more charts more flexibly and conveniently, truly achieving "unlimited possibilities in charting"!
Feature Details
1. Brand New Default Theme
During the development of ECharts 6.0, we analyzed real user scenarios and found that over 70% of developers use the default theme. This made us realize: an excellent default theme should not only be aesthetically pleasing but also meet the general needs of various business scenarios.
The new theme system uses design tokens to reconstruct colors, spacing, and other design elements,
making different chart types and components more harmonious and consistent
.
Although the 6.0 theme has significant changes from 5.x, we provide a
v5.js
theme file for developers who want to use new features but keep the old style for quick migration.
2. Dynamic Theme Switching
In previous versions, changing a chart's theme required disposing of the chart instance and re-initializing, which could negatively impact user experience due to repeated animations. In the new version, we implemented
dynamic theme switching
(see documentation), significantly improving the user experience.
3. Dark Mode Support
With dynamic theme registration and switching, a typical scenario is
listening to the system's dark mode and dynamically adjusting the chart's theme
.
